extracted.intended_audience: school and postsecondary institution administrators, Title IX coordinators, campus compliance officers, and legal counsel responsible for Title IX implementation
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for (1) confidentiality and disclosure of supportive measures (including FERPA and federal-award reporting interactions), (2) consultation requirements for students with disabilities, and (3) standards and guardrails for emergency removal of respondents under Title IX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on disclosure of supportive measures (§106.44(g)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department modified §106.44(g)(5) to prohibit disclosures about supportive measures to persons other than the persons to whom the supportive measures apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prohibition is intended to protect parties' willingness to seek supportive measures; disclosure to another party about someone else's supportive measure is expected to be restricted except where an exception applies. The final rule combined sentences from the NPRM for clarity and removed redundant phrasing. Example: a respondent who already knows the complainant's identity is not entitled to know that the complainant is receiving counseling services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinct scope of §106.44(j) nondisclosure vs §106.44(g)(5)
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.44(j) applies to personally identifiable information obtained in complying with this part; §106.44(g)(5) applies to any information about supportive measures (not just personally identifiable information).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even where identity is known through grievance procedures, the information about the supportive measure itself is protected (e.g., that a complainant is receiving counseling). §106.44(g)(5) was retained in addition to §106.44(j) because of considerations specific to supportive measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to nondisclosure (incorporation of §106.44(j)(1)-(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.44(g)(5) permits disclosure of information about supportive measures if one of the exceptions in §106.44(j)(1)–(5) applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of exceptions include prior written consent from the person receiving the supportive measure (§106.44(j)(1)); disclosures to parents of minors in elementary/secondary school (§106.44(j)(2)); and disclosures required by Federal laws/regulations or terms and conditions of a Federal award (§106.44(j)(4)). The Department incorporated these exceptions explicitly to avoid conflict between provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: FERPA interaction for disclosures of supportive measures
rubrics_metrics.description: FERPA permits disclosure of personally identifiable information from a student's education records without consent to other school officials whom the recipient has determined have a legitimate educational interest (34 CFR 99.7(a)(3)(iii), 99.31(a)(1)(i)(A)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERPA does not necessarily preclude disclosure of supportive-measure information to school officials when necessary to provide the supportive measure, but even if FERPA would permit such disclosure, recipients should only inform one party of supportive measures provided to another party when necessary to restore or preserve access to the education program or activity. Recipients must define 'legitimate educational interest' in their annual FERPA notification (34 CFR 99.7(a)(3)(iii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Wording change to protect non-complainants
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department replaced the phrase 'complainant or respondent' with 'the person to whom they apply' in §106.44(g)(5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change ensures that protective limits on disclosure encompass supportive measures provided to persons who do not make complaints (i.e., broadens coverage beyond parties who file grievances).

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator consultation with IEP/Section 504 teams (§106.44(g)(6)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient must require the Title IX Coordinator to consult with one or more members, as appropriate, of a student's IEP team or Section 504 team when implementing supportive measures for elementary and secondary students with disabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consultation requirement is intended to address intersections between supportive measures and decisions about placement, reasonable accommodations, or special education/related services; it does not require full IEP or Section 504 meetings, does not mandate specific individuals be included, and does not specify decisionmaking processes. The recipient bears responsibility for ensuring consultation occurs and may convene fuller meetings if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and limits of consultation (IDEA/Section 504 interaction)
rubrics_metrics.description: The consultation with IEP/Section 504 team members is for the purpose of determining how the recipient can comply with relevant Federal laws protecting students with disabilities while carrying out Title IX obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mere consultation with IEP/504 members may not ensure compliance with IDEA or Section 504 because those statutes operate independently; the Title IX consultation may identify additional measures necessary to ensure IDEA/504 compliance. §106.44(g)(6) does not modify rights under the ADA, IDEA, or Section 504.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to education records by Title IX Coordinator under FERPA
rubrics_metrics.description: A Title IX Coordinator's access to disability-related education records (e.g., IEPs, Section 504 plans) is permissible when such access is solely in connection with implementation of supportive measures and may constitute a legitimate educational interest under FERPA (34 CFR 99.31(a)(1)(i)(A)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should treat such access as limited to the implementation needs for supportive measures and must include criteria for what they consider 'legitimate educational interest' in their annual FERPA notification (34 CFR 99.7(a)(3)(iii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency removal standard: 'imminent and serious' threat (§106.44(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may remove a respondent on an emergency basis when, after an individualized safety and risk analysis, the recipient determines the respondent poses an imminent and serious threat to the health or safety of a complainant or any students, employees, or other persons arising from allegations of sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department replaced 'immediate' with 'imminent' to align with threat-assessment practice: 'immediate' denotes circumstances requiring law enforcement response with no time to assess, while 'imminent' denotes a risk likely to occur soon and appropriate for individualized assessment. The standard covers serious non-physical threats (e.g., stalking) as well as physical threats. Emergency removal is intended only where justified by an imminent and serious threat and is not meant as a tool to address ordinary allegations of sex discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guardrails and procedural protections for emergency removal
rubrics_metrics.description: The emergency removal provision contains requirements that recipients must: (1) undertake an individualized safety and risk analysis; (2) determine that an imminent and serious threat to health or safety arising from the allegations justifies removal; and (3) provide the respondent with notice and an opportunity to challenge the decision immediately following the removal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These protections are intended to balance campus safety and respondent rights. Emergency removal is not intended to be permanent; permanent expulsion or removal requires implementation of grievance procedures under §106.45 (and §106.46 if applicable). The Department declined to prescribe additional procedural specifics (e.g., exact post-removal procedures or maximum time limits) and left flexibility to recipients, noting many already have compliant procedures. The term used for the assessment may vary (e.g., 'threat assessment').

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope: emergency removal applies to all forms of sex discrimination but must respect speech/First Amendment protections
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.44(h) applies to sex discrimination broadly (not limited to sex-based harassment), but the Department expects that speech which merely articulates viewpoints will not meet the high standard of 'imminent and serious threat' required for emergency removal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must avoid using emergency-removal authority to punish or silence protected speech. The Department reaffirmed that Title IX is enforced consistent with First Amendment protections and does not expect viewpoint speech that is offensive or objectionable to justify removal absent an imminent and serious threat to safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial emergency removals and supportive measures that burden respondents
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may remove a respondent on an emergency basis from part of a recipient's education program or activity (e.g., certain classes, teams, or organizations) rather than the entire program or activity, where the standards for emergency removal are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partial removals may mitigate the burden on respondents while addressing safety risks. The Department acknowledged commenters' concerns about alternative access (classes, work) but did not mandate specific accommodations; recipients have discretion to tailor removals and to provide alternative access as appropriate. Emergency removal is different from ordinary supportive measures that may burden a respondent; the availability of emergency removal from part of a program was affirmed from the 2020 amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-derogation of parental or legal representative rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the supportive-measures nondisclosure provision can be read to derogate any legal right of a parent, guardian, or other authorized legal representative to act on behalf of a complainant, respondent, or other person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must respect applicable parental or guardian legal rights (including acting in connection with supportive measures) consistent with other regulatory provisions (and the FERPA and IDEA/Section 504 frameworks where applicable).
